successors.name: South Africa
successors.text: the Bophuthatswana homeland: six enclaves at independence, seven by 1994 (Mmabatho, Ga-Rankuwa and Mabopane, Mathanjana, Thaba 'Nchu, the Rustenburg area and one more in the Free State); the pages…

ledger.x: 6 December 1977: Bophuthatswana is declared 'independent' under Lucas Mangope; only South Africa and Transkei recognised it.
1980: Mafeking is incorporated after a local referendum ('Mafeking, just outside the borders at independence, was incorporated after a local referendum.
27 April 1994: Bophuthatswana is reincorporated into South Africa.

27 April 1994: the homeland ends after the March 1994 crisis (Mangope deposed on 12 March) and passes to the provinces of the new South Africa; infobox 'Dissolved: 27 April 1994', 'Succeeded by: South Africa'.

wars.name: 1988 Bophuthatswana coup attempt
wars.outcome: Coup of 10 February 1988 by Rocky Malebane-Metsing; South African Defence Force troops 'invaded and reinstated Mangope'.

wars.name: 1994 Bophuthatswana crisis
wars.outcome: 9-11 March 1994: Afrikaner right-wing groups mobilised at Mangope's invitation to Constand Viljoen, and AWB members shot at civilians near Mmabatho/Mafikeng and were repelled; on 12 March the South African government and the Transitional Executive Council…

certainty.note: The homeland's limits were statutory (the Status of Bophuthatswana Act of 1977), so the edge is sharp; but the dossier draws the enclaves as discs because no page gives an outline, so the shape is approximate.
